samples.summary: The 'doc' (Tree/CRDT) copy arm is only tested with an EMPTY source root, so no test proves docs content is actually copied
samples.evidence: `it('routes a doc through the Tree serializer…')` builds the service with `sourceRoot: {}` and asserts only `expect(targetRoot.content).toBeDefined()`. With an empty root, `readDocsRoot({})` returns `{ blocks: [] }` (docs-tree.ts:427-431) and `writeDocsRoot` unconditionally does `root.content = new Tree({type:'doc',children:[]})` (docs-tree.ts:517-528). So `targetRoot.content` is defined no matter what content the source had — the assertion holds even if the read/write dropped every block, header, footer, pageSetup and stylesJson. Contrast with the sheet arm, which is tested with a real populated root (`expect(targetRoot).toEqual(sourceRoot)`). No test in the file passes a non-empty docs root.

samples.summary: The `note` copy branch (readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `copyContent` has three distinct arms: `doc`, `note`, and the JSON_ROOT_TYPES snapshot path. The spec exercises `sheet` (JSON) and `doc`, but a grep for `note` in document-copy.service.spec.ts returns no matches. A note copy that silently produced an empty `Text`, used the wrong docKeyPrefix, or skipped the write entirely would ship green.

samples.summary: The Yorkie stand-in ignores the document id, so no test can catch reading from / writing to the wrong document
samples.evidence: `makeYorkie` distinguishes the read attach from the write attach purely by `opts?.syncMode === 'readonly'` and never inspects `_id`. Nothing in the suite asserts `withDocument` was called with `sourceId` for the read and `created.id` for the write, nor with the correct `docKeyPrefix`. Swapping `sourceId`/`targetId` in `copyContent` (service.ts:139/143, 160/164, 180/188) — which would overwrite the source or copy the target onto itself — would leave every test green.
searchedFor: grep for 'docKeyPrefix' assertions in the spec

samples.summary: No test covers copying a document with `folderId: null` (root of workspace)
samples.evidence: `copy` conditionally spreads `folder: { connect: … }` only when `source.folderId` is truthy, and `copyTitle` de-dups against `documents({ where: { folderId: null } })`. Every test in the spec uses `SOURCE` with `folderId: 'fld-1'` (or spreads it), so the null-folder branch — which is the common case for workspace-root documents — is never executed.
searchedFor: read SOURCE fixture and all test cases in document-copy.service.spec.ts

samples.summary: `copyDocument` API helper has no test, though its sibling helpers do

The new POST /documents/:id/copy call shape and its `assertOk` error message are untested.

samples.summary: Bulk-copy mutation behavior (sequential copies, partial-failure refetch, folder ids excluded) is untested
samples.evidence: `copyDocumentsMutation` adds non-trivial behavior: sequential `for (const id of ids) await copyDocument(id)`, `onSettled: invalidateLists()` justified in a comment as covering partial failure, and a bar button gated on `selectedDocIds.length > 0` to exclude folders. No test file under packages/frontend/src/app/documents/ covers document-list mutations (only miro-import / apply-imported-content tests exist), so the partial-failure claim in the comment is asserted nowhere.

samples.summary: 'only considers the titles it is given' asserts nothing the first test does not already assert
samples.evidence: The case is `expect(copyTitle('Report', [])).toBe('Report (copy)')`, while the first test already covers `copyTitle('Report', ['Report'])`. The comment claims it proves titles from another folder/workspace never bump the number, but `copyTitle` has no knowledge of folders — the actual scoping lives in the service's `documents({ where: … })` query. The test name/comment overstate what is verified.

samples.summary: No test that FileService.copy propagates an S3 failure, which the service's rollback contract depends on
samples.evidence: The shared `mockSend` is `jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({})` and is never made to reject in any `FileService.copy` test. DocumentCopyService's `discardBlob`/rollback ordering assumes a failed `copy()` rejects before a row is created; the rejecting path is never exercised at the FileService level.

verdict.reason: Real but not blocking under this lens's rubric, and the vacuity argument is factually wrong. (1) The doc-arm assertion is NOT true regardless of behavior: the JSON arm returns early on an empty snapshot (document-copy.service.ts:187, proved by the sibling test at spec:109-115 asserting exactly one attach), so a 'doc' mis-routed to the JSON arm or to the blob no-op would leave targetRoot === {} and expect(targetRoot.content).toBeDefined() would fail. The test pins exactly the routing its title claims. (2) The doc arm's entire behavior is readDocsRoot(source) then writeDocsRoot(target, content) (document-copy.service.ts:136-151), and content preservation through that exact pair is covered with real populated content in docs-tree.spec.ts: simple round-trip (58-65), table cell borders with comma-containing colors (98-159), pageSetup and stylesJson including clearing on omission (161-213), header/footer regions preserved (215-265), and a 'fully-populated document with byte-equal shape' asserting blocks, headings, list items, tables, images, pageSetup, header and footer all equal (323-551). The precise failure the finding hypothesizes -- that the read/write dropped every block, header, footer, pageSetup and stylesJson -- is directly falsified by those tests. I did confirm no copy-path test uses a populated docs root (zero 'copy' matches in packages/backend/test; document.controller.spec.ts:458-505 mocks copyService.copy entirely), so the untested residue is only the threading of the content variable between two independently proven calls, which the routing test does exercise with an empty document. That is the rubric's 'minor -- coverage could be broader but the core behavior is tested' case, and the rubric forbids treating 'add more tests' as a blocker unless a real behavior change genuinely lacks any meaningful test.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `copyContent` in document-copy.service.ts has a dedicated `note` arm (lines 155-174) using yorkieDocKeyPrefix('note') plus readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot, distinct from the `doc` arm (134-153) and the JSON_ROOT_TYPES snapshot arm (176-198). Reading document-copy.service.spec.ts in full shows tests for `sheet`, `doc`, `pdf`, empty-root skip, and rollback — none invoke service.copy with type 'note'. Searching wider for a counterexample: document.controller.spec.ts:458-505 mocks copyService.copy outright so no arm is reached; grep for 'copy' across packages/backend/test/** (all e2e suites) returns zero matches, so no integration test hits the copy path; a repo-wide grep for DocumentCopyService/copyContent finds only the one spec; and repo-wide grep for `type: 'note'` in test files yields only cli notes-import, docs-content.controller.spec, and yorkie-doc-key.spec, none of which touch the copy service. The closest candidate, packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.spec.ts, unit-tests readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot against a fake Text but never goes through copyContent, so it cannot catch a wrong docKeyPrefix, a skipped target write, a wrong syncMode, or the note arm failing to route. A distinct new behavior arm ships with no meaningful test while its structural twin (`doc`) got one — major under the missing-tests lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. The `withDocument` stand-in at document-copy.service.spec.ts:23-37 takes `_id` and never reads it; it selects the read arm purely by `opts?.syncMode === 'readonly'` (line 29) and ignores `docKeyPrefix`. The suite contains no `toHaveBeenCalledWith` for the spy at all — only `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` (line 114), `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 147) and `mockRejectedValue` (line 168). Consequently, swapping `sourceId`/`targetId` in copyContent (service.ts:139/143, 160/164, 179/188) — which would copy the target onto itself or overwrite the source — leaves every assertion green, including `expect(targetRoot).toEqual(sourceRoot)` (line 106) and `targetRoot.content` (line 122), because the mock's arms are keyed on syncMode rather than id. No coverage exists elsewhere: document.controller.spec.ts:458-503 mocks `copyService.copy` wholesale, yorkie.service.spec.ts tests withDocument in isolation, and no e2e test exercises copy. This is over-mocking that renders the feature's core routing behavior untestable, squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by impact.
